title: Understanding k-fold Cross Validation
text: In k-fold cross-validation, the dataset is divided into k subsets, and the model is trained and validated k times, each time using a different subset as the validation set and the remaining as the training set.

title: Bias and Variance in Cross Validation
text: Increasing k in k-fold cross-validation generally reduces the variance of the model's performance estimate, but how does it affect bias?

hintAnswer: Increasing k decreases the bias of the model.
title: Effect of Increasing k on Bias
text: Consider how using more folds (increasing k) affects the amount of data used for training in each iteration. Does this lead to a more or less biased model?
choices: Increasing k decreases the bias of the model.

title: Computational Intensity of Cross Validation
text: Cross-validation is generally more computationally intensive than regular validation because it involves training the model multiple times.

hintAnswer: $$Cross-validation$$ allows us to use the entire training dataset to test the model, providing a more reliable estimate of model performance.
title: Why Use Cross Validation?
text: Why might we prefer cross-validation over regular validation despite its computational cost?
choices: $$Cross-validation$$ allows us to use the entire training dataset to test the model, providing a more reliable estimate of model performance.

title: Cross Validation in Production
text: Consider whether cross-validation is suitable for use in a production environment, where the model should not have access to validation samples.

hintAnswer: $$Cross-validation$$ is not suitable for production because the model is evaluated on data it has already seen during training, which can lead to overfitting.
title: Cross Validation and Model Cheating
text: Why might cross-validation be considered 'cheating' if used in production?
choices: $$Cross-validation$$ is not suitable for production because the model is evaluated on data it has already seen during training, which can lead to overfitting.
